# Listening: map-label strategy and route tracking

**Source:** [Band 9 Strategy for IELTS Listening Maps [+ Free Listening PDF]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-aBW-RHtcrE), video ID `-aBW-RHtcrE`. Full auto-generated English captions were exported and reviewed through 30:28. The lesson overlaps the map section in the full Listening course; its main added value is a highly explicit preview-and-visualize routine followed by two worked maps.

## Reusable procedure

1. **Read the instructions.** Identify the required answer format and word limit. In the lesson’s examples the task asks for a letter, so write the corresponding letter rather than the name of the place. ([0:28–1:08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-aBW-RHtcrE&t=28s))
2. **Orient yourself on the map.** Name the main features, paths, gates, roads, and likely landmarks. Check compass directions, labels, and which way the speaker is facing if shown. Keep unfamiliar objects in context; the task is to connect the description with the map, not to know specialist facts. ([1:08–1:49](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-aBW-RHtcrE&t=68s); [10:40–12:05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-aBW-RHtcrE&t=640s))
3. **Preview the choices and gaps.** For each target, predict the kind of place or facility, nearby landmarks, plausible route language, and likely paraphrases. A café might be called a coffee shop; a path may be described with several related terms. Treat these as hypotheses only—do not let a prediction override what the recording says. ([1:49–5:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-aBW-RHtcrE&t=109s))
4. **Identify the starting point.** Listen closely to the opening for the entry gate, current position, orientation, and general context. “On your right” depends on where the route begins and which way the speaker is facing. ([5:40–7:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-aBW-RHtcrE&t=340s))
5. **Travel the route mentally.** Follow turn instructions and route markers in sequence: continue, turn, pass, cross, go beyond, stand opposite, go between, or return. Imagine moving from one mapped position to the next; use the named landmarks to keep your place. ([5:40–8:14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-aBW-RHtcrE&t=340s))
6. **Track time and status.** Separate what is there now from what used to be there, has moved, is closed, or is only planned for the future. A familiar place name can be a distractor if the speaker says it no longer exists. Ignore information that does not match a label or location in the actual task. ([7:17–8:14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-aBW-RHtcrE&t=437s); [15:03–16:26](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-aBW-RHtcrE&t=903s); [20:42–22:23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-aBW-RHtcrE&t=1242s))
7. **Use signposts and answer.** Phrases such as “let’s start,” “now go back,” “next,” “finally,” and “as we round” tell you where the speaker is in the route. Confirm the selected letter or label, then move attention to the next item. ([8:14–9:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-aBW-RHtcrE&t=494s))

## Practice progression and limits

When first learning the routine, replay or pause as needed and explain each answer using the speaker’s route and map evidence. Practise until the directions feel manageable; then reduce support and use fresh material under one-listen, timed test conditions. Increase speed gradually rather than using repeated playback to judge exam readiness. ([9:10–10:24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-aBW-RHtcrE&t=550s))

IELTS Listening map-label questions ask the candidate to match information from the recording to locations on a map, and the task instructions determine the response form. Use the current [official Listening format](https://ielts.org/take-a-test/test-types/ielts-academic-test/ielts-academic-format-listening) for exam facts. The instructor’s “thousands of students,” Band 9/full-marks outcomes, “exact” strategy wording, and claims that any student applying the routine will outperform a stronger listener are not independently verified. The practice questions are presented by the video, but their source and status as official materials are not established here. ([0:00–0:28](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-aBW-RHtcrE&t=0s); [5:17–5:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-aBW-RHtcrE&t=317s))
